headline: 85 detained as police raid 'drug parties' at addl DIG's house in Dhaka
summary: The house, owned by Additional DIG Abdullah Al Zahir, reportedly hosted parties 20 days a month with loud music and drugs.
details: Police raided a rented house in Dhaka’s Khilkhet owned by Additional Deputy Inspector General Abdullah Al Zahir on Monday. The operation led to the detention of 85 people, including 26 women, who were found engaging in loud music, dancing, and drug use.
Alcohol, yaba, kush, and shisha equipment were recovered from the premises, according to Dhaka Metropolitan Police Uttara Division Deputy Commissioner Ilias Kabir.
The participants, which included university students, bankers, and children of law enforcement personnel, reportedly registered for the events via Airbnb and Travela.
Investigations revealed that parties occurred 20 to 22 times a month. Some guests paid up to Tk 18,500 to rent the venue, while others paid Tk 600 each.
Additional DIG Abdullah Al Zahir has been made an officer on special duty (OSD) and attached to police headquarters following the incident.
Zahir claimed he did not organize the events and had appointed a manager to oversee the house, instructing him to follow all rules.
The detained men were sentenced to one month in jail and a Tk 1,000 fine, while women received 15 days in jail and a Tk 500 fine.
caption:
85 people detained in a raid on a high-ranking police officer's house used for 'drug parties'.

Police raided a rented house in Dhaka’s Khilkhet owned by Additional Deputy Inspector General Abdullah Al Zahir on Monday. The operation led to the detention of 85 people, including 26 women, who were found engaging in loud music, dancing, and drug use.

Alcohol, yaba, kush, and shisha equipment were recovered from the premises, according to Dhaka Metropolitan Police Uttara Division Deputy Commissioner Ilias Kabir.

The participants, which included university students, bankers, and children of law enforcement personnel, reportedly registered for the events via Airbnb and Travela.

Investigations revealed that parties occurred 20 to 22 times a month. Some guests paid up to Tk 18,500 to rent the venue, while others paid Tk 600 each.

Additional DIG Abdullah Al Zahir has been made an officer on special duty (OSD) and attached to police headquarters following the incident.

Zahir claimed he did not organize the events and had appointed a manager to oversee the house, instructing him to follow all rules.

The detained men were sentenced to one month in jail and a Tk 1,000 fine, while women received 15 days in jail and a Tk 500 fine.

headline_marked: 7-wicket loss to Afghanistan: [[Bangladesh bow out of tri-series]]
headline: 7-wicket loss to Afghanistan: Bangladesh bow out of tri-series
summary: Another batting collapse in Sharjah sees the Tigers slump to 160, ending their hopes of reaching the final.
details: Bangladesh's hopes of reaching the tri-series final ended in another batting collapse, as Afghanistan chased down 161 with 7 wickets and 87 balls to spare in Sharjah.
Stand-in captain Towhid Hridoy chose to bat first, but the top order crumbled. Tanzid Hasan and Soumya Sarkar fell cheaply, leaving the team at 6 for 2, while Hridoy himself fell for a duck.
A 93-run partnership between Saif Hassan (41) and Parvez Hossain Emon (70) steadied the innings, but the acceleration failed to materialize.
Rashid Khan tore through the tail, dismissing Shoriful Islam and Parvez, then removing Aliss Al Islam and Mustafizur Rahman with successive deliveries to end the innings at 160.
Taskin Ahmed provided a glimmer of hope with 2 for 36, dismissing Rahmanullah Gurbaz and Sediqullah Atal early on.
However, an unbeaten 66-run stand between Rahmat Shah (67*) and Hashmatullah Shahidi (36*) sealed the victory for Afghanistan in 35.3 overs.
This marks Bangladesh's fifth successive ODI defeat by Afghanistan and their second loss of the tournament after an opening defeat to Zimbabwe.
caption:
Another batting collapse in Sharjah. Bangladesh is out of the tri-series.

Bangladesh's hopes of reaching the tri-series final ended in another batting collapse, as Afghanistan chased down 161 with 7 wickets and 87 balls to spare in Sharjah.

Stand-in captain Towhid Hridoy chose to bat first, but the top order crumbled. Tanzid Hasan and Soumya Sarkar fell cheaply, leaving the team at 6 for 2, while Hridoy himself fell for a duck.

A 93-run partnership between Saif Hassan (41) and Parvez Hossain Emon (70) steadied the innings, but the acceleration failed to materialize.

Rashid Khan tore through the tail, dismissing Shoriful Islam and Parvez, then removing Aliss Al Islam and Mustafizur Rahman with successive deliveries to end the innings at 160.

Taskin Ahmed provided a glimmer of hope with 2 for 36, dismissing Rahmanullah Gurbaz and Sediqullah Atal early on.

However, an unbeaten 66-run stand between Rahmat Shah (67*) and Hashmatullah Shahidi (36*) sealed the victory for Afghanistan in 35.3 overs.

This marks Bangladesh's fifth successive ODI defeat by Afghanistan and their second loss of the tournament after an opening defeat to Zimbabwe.
